facts.statement: Bergisuchus was first discovered in 1966 by Dr. Dietrich Berg in the Messel Pit, Germany.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus was first discovered by Dr. Dietrich Berg from the German Messel Pit in 1966

facts.statement: The genus was formally named and described in 1968 by the German paleontologist Oskar Kuhn.
facts.quote: It was named and described two years later in 1968 by German palaeontologist Oskar Kuhn

facts.statement: Kuhn named the species *Bergisuchus dietrichbergi* to honor Dr. Berg and used the Greek suffix *suchos* meaning 'crocodile'.
facts.quote: who named the binomial Bergisuchus dietrichbergi in honour of Dr. Berg and combined it with the Greek suffix suchos for "crocodile"

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, a snout and lower jaw, was found in the Messel Pit near Darmstadt and reported in 1966.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus is known from the holotype snout and lower jaw (HLMD-Me 7003) from the Messel Pit near Darmstadt first reported in 1966

facts.statement: An additional incomplete pair of lower jaws was found in the Geiseltal coal mine near Halle, Saxony-Anhalt.
facts.quote: and an additional incomplete pair of mandibles (GM XVIII-49) from the Geiseltal open-pit coal mine near Halle in the state of Saxony-Anhalt from the slightly younger MP 12

facts.statement: In 2015, osteoderms from Middle Eocene deposits in Lissieu, France, were tentatively attributed to *Bergisuchus*.
facts.quote: In 2015, osteoderms from karst deposits dated to the Middle Eocene in Lissieu, France, were tentatively suggested to belong to Bergisuchus sp.

facts.statement: *Bergisuchus* possessed a snout shape quite different from the broad, flat snouts of modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: quite unlike the broad flat snouts of modern crocodylians

facts.statement: Researchers suggest *Bergisuchus* was likely a fast, terrestrial predator rather than an aquatic ambush hunter.
facts.quote: As with other sebecosuchians, it is likely that Bergisuchus was a fast, terrestrial predator and not an aquatic ambush hunter like modern crocodylians

facts.statement: *Bergisuchus* had a tall, laterally compressed snout with tall nasals forming a raised, sharp midline.
facts.quote: The snout is tall and laterally compressed, unlike the broad flat snouts of modern crocodylians, with tall nasals that form a raised, sharp midline along the length of the snout

facts.statement: *Bergisuchus* had relatively narrow, serrated teeth similar to predatory theropod dinosaurs, unlike the conical teeth of modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: The teeth are relatively narrow and serrated (ziphodont), similar to those of predatory theropod dinosaurs and unlike the conical teeth of modern crocodylians

facts.statement: The large lower canine tooth of *Bergisuchus* was approximately 2 cm tall and sat on a raised portion of the jaw bone.
facts.quote: This canine is approximately 2 cm tall, and sits on a prominently raised portion of the jaw bone

facts.statement: *Bergisuchus* lived during the Early to Middle Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle EoceneEarly to Middle

facts.statement: *Bergisuchus* is known primarily from the Eocene Messel Pit in Germany.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus is an extinct genus of small sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian known primarily from the Eocene Messel Pit in Germany

facts.statement: *Bergisuchus* indicates that sebecosuchians were once more widespread in Europe than later in the Cenozoic, when they were restricted to South America.
facts.quote: Its presence in Europe is also unusual, as later sebecosuchians were restricted entirely to South America

facts.statement: The species was named *Bergisuchus dietrichbergi* by Oskar Kuhn in 1968.
facts.quote: It was named and described two years later in 1968 by German palaeontologist Oskar Kuhn, who named the binomial Bergisuchus dietrichbergi

facts.statement: In 2000, Rossmann and colleagues assigned *Bergisuchus* to its own monotypic family, the Bergisuchidae, based on its distinctness from *Sebecus*.
facts.quote: In 2000, the sebecosuchian affinities of Bergisuchus, particularly to Sebecus, were established by Rossmann and colleagues in a thorough re-examination of the material, and it was assigned to its own monotypic family, the Bergisuchidae

facts.statement: While phylogenetic analyses support *Bergisuchus* as a close relative of *Sebecus*, the exact interrelationships between *Bergisuchus*, Sebecidae, and other clades remain unsettled.
facts.quote: The position of Bergisuchus as a close relative of Sebecus has since been supported by a number of phylogenetic analyses of Mesozoic and Cenozoic mesoeucrocodylians, although the interrelationships of Bergisuchus, Sebecidae and other clades are not settled

facts.statement: Different phylogenetic analyses have produced conflicting results, with some excluding *Bergisuchus* from Sebecidae and others placing it well within the family.
facts.quote: The former analysis found Bergisuchus and Iberosuchus as sebecosuchians closely related to but excluded from Sebecidae, while the latter analysis recovers Bergisuchus well within Sebecidae

facts.statement: Bergisuchus is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylian belonging to the sebecosuchian group.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus es un género extinto de mesoeucrocodilio sebecosuquio.

facts.statement: Bergisuchus was a small terrestrial hypercarnivore.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus era un pequeño hipercarnívoro terrestre.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the front-heavy teeth of Bergisuchus were a specialization for hunting large prey by delivering powerful bites at the jaw's front.
facts.quote: This has been suggested to be a specialisation for hunting large-sized prey items by imparting more powerful bites at the very front of the jaws.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Bergisuchus used large front canines as fangs and smaller rear teeth to chew food before swallowing.
facts.quote: They suggested that Bergisuchus used the large canines at the front of the jaws as fangs and the smaller rear teeth to "chew" and process food before swallowing.

facts.statement: Huge, exaggerated canines in Bergisuchus may have functioned as sexual signals or weapons in intraspecific competition rather than for predation.
facts.quote: They also suggested that the huge, exaggerated canines could possibly have been used as sexual signals or as weapons in intraspecific competition, rather than predation.

facts.statement: Bergisuchus fossils have been found at the Messel fossil site in Germany, dating to the Eocene.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han encontrado en el sitio fosilífero de Messel en Alemania, que data del Eoceno.

facts.statement: Bergisuchus lived during the Lutetian stage, between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: Bergisuchus was originally classified as a sebecosuchian, supposedly the first found outside South America, and later assigned to Trematochampsidae in 1988.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus fue clasificado originalmente como un sebecosuquio, supuestamente el primero hallado por fuera de Suramérica, y más tarde asignado a Trematochampsidae en 1988.

facts.statement: The Messel site is famous for well-preserved fossils including semi-aquatic crocodylomorphs like Asiatosuchus and Diplocynodon.
facts.quote: El sitio de Messel es famoso por sus bien preservados fósiles, los cuales incluyen crocodilomorfos semiacuáticos como Asiatosuchus y Diplocynodon.

facts.statement: Bergisuchus is known from a holotype rostrum from Messel described in 1966 and a jaw found in an open-pit coal mine near Halle in Saxony-Anhalt.
facts.quote: Bergisuchus es conocido a partir del fósil holotipo, un rostrum proveniente de Messel, descrito originalmente en 1966, y una mandíbula hallada en una mina a cielo abierto de carbón cerca de Halle en el estado de Sajonia-Anhalt.

facts.statement: The family Bergisuchidae was established by Rossmann et al. in 2000.
facts.quote: familia_authority: Rossmann et al., 2000

facts.statement: The genus Bergisuchus was established by Berg in 1966.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Berg, 1966

facts.statement: The species B. dietrichbergi was described by Kuhn in 1968.
facts.quote: subdivision: B. dietrichbergi Kuhn, 1968

facts.statement: Rossmann and colleagues extensively speculated about the paleoecology of Bergisuchus.
facts.quote: Rossmann and colleagues speculated extensively about the palaeoecology of Bergisuchus.

facts.statement: Researchers interpreted rare, fragmented Bergisuchus bones as evidence they were transported into Messel and Geiseltal sites from elsewhere, unlike the abundant, well-preserved crocodylians found there.
facts.quote: They interpreted the rare, fragmented material as evidence for the bones being transported into these settings from elsewhere, compared to the more abundant and more complete crocodylians from these sites that were well preserved by the local conditions.

facts.statement: The presence of Bergisuchus in Europe is regarded as evidence for a connection between South American and European faunas in the early Eocene, though this is debated.
facts.quote: The presence of Bergisuchus in Europe has been regarded as evidence for a connection between the faunas from South America and Europe in the early Eocene, as other Cenozoic sebecosuchians are mostly known from South America.

facts.statement: It is suggested that Bergisuchus descended from a separate invasion from South America during the Palaeogene rather than from Cretaceous European sebecosuchians like Doratodon.
facts.quote: This appears to indicate that Bergisuchus and other European sebecosuchians did not descend from Cretaceous European sebecosuchians like Doratodon, but was instead part of a separate invasion of sebecosuchians into Europe during the Palaeogene from South America.

facts.statement: In 2000, Bergisuchus was given its own family, Bergisuchidae, of which it is the only representative.
facts.quote: En 2000, al género le fue dado su propia familia, Bergisuchidae, de la que es su único representante.
